settings.name_in_paper: Bandit tree search (max search in binary tree of depth D, leaves with [0,1] rewards)
unmapped: Arms are the 2^D leaves of a binary tree of depth D; trajectories select a leaf by walking from root
Learner knows the tree depth D (and number of nodes N = 2^{D+1}-1)
settings.definition_quote: Let a binary tree of depth $D$ where at each leaf $i$ is assigned a random variable $X_i$, with bounded support $[0,1]$, whose law is unknown. Successive visits of a leaf $i$ yield a sequence of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) samples

unmapped: Leaves of a binary tree of depth D; smoothness assumption: for any node i of depth d and leaf j below it, mu_i - mu_j <= delta_d
Learner knows the smoothness coefficients delta_d and the number of nodes N
settings.definition_quote: Smoothness assumption: Assume that for all depth $d<D$, there exists $\delta_d>0$, such that for any node $i$ of depth $d$, for all leaves $j\in\L(i)$ in the branch $i$, we have $\mu_i - \mu_j \leq \delta_d$.

settings.name_in_paper: Growing (incremental) tree search in possibly infinite trees
unmapped: Tree expanded incrementally; reward from leaf j at depth d has mean within delta_d of the node value mu_j
Exponential smoothness delta_d = delta*gamma^d known to learner
settings.definition_quote: We make an assumption on the rewards: from any leaf $j$, the received reward $x$ is a random variable whose expected value satisfies: $ \mu_j - \E[x] \leq \delta_d$, where $d$ is the depth of $j$

symbols.D_depth: depth of the binary tree (K = 2^D_depth leaves)

source.label: thm:modified-uct
source.quote: Let $\beta>0$. Consider Algorithm \ref{alg:BATS} with the upper confidence bound (\ref{eq:modified-uct}). Then, with probability at least $1-\beta$, for all $n\geq 1$, the pseudo-regret is bounded by \bar R_n\leq \frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}\big[(1+\sqrt{2})^D-1\big] \sqrt{2\log(\beta_{n}^{-1})n} + \frac{3^D-1}{2}

results.notes: delta = paper's beta; beta_n^{-1} = 2N n(n+1)/beta substituted. Pseudo-regret defined as sum_j n_j Delta_j.

symbols.D_depth: depth of the binary tree (K = 2^D_depth leaves)

source.label: thm:flat-ucb
source.quote: Consider the flat UCB defined by Algorithm \ref{alg:BATS} and (\ref{eq:flat-ucb}). Then, with probability at least $1-\beta$, the pseudo-regret is bounded by a constant: $$ \bar R_n \leq 40 \sum_{i\in \S} \frac{1}{\Delta_i}\log(\frac{2^{D+1}}{\Delta_i^2\beta}) \leq 40 \frac{2^D}{\Delta}\log(\frac{2^{D+1}}{\Delta^2\beta}),$$

results.notes: Bound independent of n; holds for all n on the high-probability event.

symbols.D_depth: depth of the binary tree (K = 2^D_depth leaves)

results.notes: Paper's Delta is the minimum positive gap.

symbols.N_i: recursively defined count: for leaves 40 log(2N/(beta Delta_i^2))/Delta_i^2; for internal nodes N_{i1}+N_{i2}, or min with 40 log(2N/(beta (Delta_i-delta_{d_i})^2))/(Delta_i-delta_{d_i})^2 if Delta_i > delta_{d_i}
symbols.n_i: number of visits of sub-optimal node i

source.label: thm:BAST1
source.quote: Let $I$ denotes the set of nodes i such that $\Delta_i>\delta_{d_i}$ ... Then, with probability $1-\beta$, for all $n\geq 1$, for all sub-optimal nodes $i$, $n_i\leq N_i$.

results.notes: Bound on visit counts of sub-optimal nodes, not directly a regret bound.

symbols.I_eta: |I_eta|, number of sub-optimal leaves with gap <= eta_thr
symbols.delta_s: smoothness constant delta in delta_d <= delta*gamma^d
symbols.N_nodes: number of nodes in the tree

source.quote: Consider the exponential assumption on the smoothness coefficients : $\delta_d \leq \delta \gamma^d$. For any $\eta\geq 0$ define the set of leaves $I_\eta\eqdef\{i\in \S, \Delta_i\leq \eta\}$. Then, with probability at least $1-\beta$, the pseudo regret satisfies, for all $n\geq 1$, ... \leq 40|I_\eta| \Big( \frac{1}{\Delta}\log(  \frac{2N}{\Delta^2\beta}) + \frac{8(2\delta)^c}{\eta^{2+c}} \log(\frac{2N}{\eta^2\beta}) \Big)

results.notes: Theorem also gives a tighter intermediate form: sum_{i in I_eta} 40/Delta_i log(2N/(beta Delta_i^2)) + |I_eta| 320(2delta)^c/eta^{2+c} log(2N/(eta^2 beta)). Only the final form recorded. Paper notes eta -> Delta gives O(1/Delta^{2+c}).

symbols.n_i: number of visits of sub-optimal node i

conditions: exponential smoothness delta_d = delta*gamma^d (implicit in proof)

source.quote: Consider this incremental tree method using Algorithm \ref{alg:BATS} defined by the bound (\ref{eq:BAST}) with the confidence interval ... Then, with probability $1-\beta$, for any sub-optimal node $i$ (of depth $d$), i.e. s.t. $\Delta_i>0$, n_i \leq 10 \Big(\frac{\delta}{c}\Big)^c \Big(\frac{2+c}{\Delta_i}\Big)^{c+2} \log(...)2^{-d}.

results.notes: n here is the number of expanded nodes (rounds), mapped to T. Bound on visit counts; derivation neglects log term in optimizing h, so constant may be approximate.
